_comment: PostgreSQL MCP Server -- Postgres MCP Pro (crystaldba/postgres-mcp), run in restricted mode.
Restricted mode parses every statement before it runs and refuses anything that is not
read-only, so the 'COMMIT; DROP TABLE users;' escape that breaks a plain read-only
transaction is rejected. Measured 2026-10-18 against a real Postgres with
scripts/probe_postgres_mcp.py: restricted mode refused all 5 write payloads and the table
kept its row; the unrestricted control run dropped it on the first payload.
Requires: uv (uvx) and DATABASE_URL. Linux and macOS: pglast, a dependency, has no Windows
wheel, so on Windows run it inside WSL or use the upstream Docker image.
'--with mcp<2' is required: postgres-mcp 0.3.0 declares mcp>=1.5.0 with no upper bound, and
mcp 2.x renamed FastMCP, so an unpinned uvx install crashes on import (checked 2026-10-18).
Install: Copy the 'postgres' key into .mcp.json under mcpServers.

_available: list_schemas              -- List the schemas in the database
list_objects              -- List tables, views, sequences and extensions in a schema
get_object_details        -- Columns, constraints and indexes of one object
execute_sql               -- Run SQL; read-only statements only in restricted mode
explain_query             -- Execution plan, optionally with hypothetical indexes
analyze_workload_indexes  -- Index recommendations for the heaviest queries
analyze_query_indexes     -- Index recommendations for up to 10 given queries
analyze_db_health         -- Buffer cache, connections, vacuum, invalid and unused indexes

security: Keep --access-mode=restricted. unrestricted allows writes and schema changes.
Restricted mode is a second guard, not the only one: connect as a database user that only
has SELECT grants, so a parser gap cannot become a write.
Never point this server at a production database with a write-capable user.
Never put credentials directly in this file -- use environment variables.
Consider using connection pooling (PgBouncer) for shared environments.
replaced_server: This recipe used @modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres up to 1.2.0. npm marks it
'Package no longer supported' at 0.6.2 and its source moved to servers-archived. Its
read-only transaction is bypassed by 'COMMIT; <write>', and the fix was never released.
